records.verbatim_quote: To further investigate how the refusal direction is suppressed, we examine the contributions of individual attention head and MLP components to the refusal direction. We quantify each component's contribution to this direction using direct feature attribution (DFA) (Makelov et al. 2024; Kissane et al. 2024): each component's direct contribution can be measured by projecting its output onto the refusal direction.

records.adversarial_note: Attn_SensWords is the closest published quantity (attention allocated to harm-bearing tokens) but (a) it is evaluated within a single model family (Llama2) across jailbreak METHODS, not across model FAMILIES as a safety score, and (b) it uses raw sensitive-word attention, not a harmful-vs-twin DIFFERENCE restricted to late layers with a fixed decision position. records.adversarial_note: GradSafe operates on PARAMETER gradients (safety-critical weight slices), not INPUT-token gradients, and is not applied cross-model as a ranking. The word-level gradient-attribution attack paper (2607.01859) is the functional-form closest match (per-word gradient contribution to the refusal decision) but it is used offensively (to find words to translate/obfuscate) across 6 models, never turned into a per-model safety score or correlated with benchmark safety.
records.positioning_sentence: GradSafe (2402.13494) attributes refusal to safety-critical PARAMETER gradients within one model family; we instead attribute the refusal margin to INPUT tokens that differ between harmful and twin prompts and use the resulting share as a per-checkpoint, cross-family safety indicator.

records.what_it_measured: Normalized Indirect Effect (NIE): the proportion of the refusal logit recovered by patching template-region (vs. instruction-region) activations from a harmless run into a harmful run, i.e. exactly 'template-site share of refusal drive.' Computed per model with an explicit normalization 'for a fair cross-model comparison', and plotted (Figure 4) across all 6 tested models, showing the template region dominates the instruction region in every model, with cross-model differences explicitly tied to safety vulnerability (models whose safety appeared stronger by refusal rate but showed high template NIE were, via TempPatch, MORE exploitable).
records.n_models_and_families: 6 models / 4 families: Gemma-2 (2b-it, 9b-it), Llama-2-7b-Chat, Llama-3 (3.2-3b-Instruct, 8B-Instruct), Mistral-7B-Instruct.

used_to_rank_models.quote: Right: Normalized indirect effects when patching activations are from two different regions (instruction v.s. template) across various LLMs, revealing that these models' safety functions are primarily anchored in the template regions.

records.adversarial_note: This is the clearest PUBLISHED match found in the whole sweep. Caveat: the cross-model comparison is presented as layered curves in Figure 4 (NIE vs. number of patched heads) plus a qualitative discussion tying higher template-reliance to greater TempPatch vulnerability, not as a single scalar NIE-per-model table correlated numerically against an external benchmark safety score. Per the verdict rule ('computes the same functional form per model AND compares or ranks models by it as a safety indicator'), this still qualifies as PUBLISHED: the paper explicitly computes NIE per model, explicitly states the normalization exists 'for a fair cross-model comparison', and explicitly uses cross-model NIE differences to explain why some models are more/less safe. This does NOT soften to ADJACENT.
records.positioning_sentence: Leong et al. (2502.13946) already establish and cross-model-compare a template-region NIE as a cause of safety vulnerability; any C9-style metric must be explicitly positioned as a re-derivation or extension of their NIE, not a novel construct.

records.what_it_measured: Zhao et al. show harmfulness and refusal are encoded by distinct directions and give layer-wise clustering/steering results (Figures 2, 4, 8, 14-15) on 3 models (Llama3-8B-Instruct, Llama2-7B-Chat, Qwen2-7B-Instruct), i.e. per-layer curves for both concepts on the same models -- but never subtract/integrate the two curves into an area/gap metric, and never use any such quantity to rank models by safety. Mohammad & Bayazit's Herald computes ONLY a harm-decodability trajectory (LDA projection onto a harm direction per layer, with 7 trajectory-shape features: slope, curvature, onset layer, monotonicity, etc.) across 4 model families (Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, OLMo2-7B, Qwen3-8B) and 8 benchmarks, but explicitly does NOT compute a paired refusal-drive curve (it distinguishes its harm-direction trajectory from Arditi's output-side refusal direction as a complementary, not combined, signal), and uses the trajectory to classify individual PROMPTS as harmful (an F1 detector), not to score/rank MODELS by safety.
records.n_models_and_families: Zhao et al.: 3 models (Llama3, Llama2, Qwen2), 3 families. Herald: 4 model families (Llama-3.1, Mistral, OLMo2, Qwen3), 8 benchmarks, plus scaling experiments 11B-70B.

used_to_rank_models.quote: The two directions also differ conceptually—refusal directions characterize generation-time behavior, while HPD directions characterize inference-time encoding of the prompt's intent.

records.adversarial_note: Confirms the iteration-1 memory note: 2507.11878 already 'concedes' that BOTH a harmfulness curve and a refusal curve can be plotted across layers on the same models, so a naive 'we plot two depth curves' framing is not novel. What remains unpublished after this sweep is (a) integrating the two curves into a single AREA/gap statistic, and (b) using that scalar to RANK models cross-family as a safety indicator -- neither Zhao et al. nor Herald do either. Herald additionally only has one curve (harm), explicitly treating refusal-direction work as a separate, uncombined axis, and uses it for prompt-level detection F1, not model-level safety ranking.
records.positioning_sentence: While Zhao et al. (2507.11878) show harmfulness and refusal are separately decodable across layers on the same models, and Mohammad & Bayazit (2609.13534) turn a harm-only depth trajectory into per-prompt detection features across four families, no prior work integrates the harmfulness- and refusal-drive curves into a single area statistic used to rank checkpoints by safety.

records.what_it_measured: Qi et al. compute per-token KL divergence between an ALIGNED model and its UNALIGNED BASE counterpart over the first output tokens -- this is the direct ancestor of the 'first tokens carry the safety decision' idea, but it is fundamentally PARENT-DEPENDENT (needs the base model) and tested on only 2 model families (Llama-2, Gemma). Yang et al. define Onset Refusal Collapse: a refusal-direction PROJECTION trajectory S_t over token positions, with a matched-pair gap G_t = S_t^IT - S_t^LRM between a reasoning model and its Instruction-Tuned counterpart -- also PARENT/counterpart-DEPENDENT, and restricted to 3 IT/LRM pairs studying a reasoning-specific failure mode, not a general parent-free cross-family safety score. Park & Kim study hidden-state trajectory redirection under token injection across 3 models (Mistral, Llama, Qwen) but as an ATTACK/robustness vulnerability analysis, not a static per-checkpoint refusal-commitment score.
records.n_models_and_families: Qi et al.: 2 (Llama-2, Gemma), each requiring its own base/aligned pair. Yang et al.: 3 IT/LRM pairs within Llama and Qwen. Park & Kim: 3 models (Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B).

used_to_rank_models.quote: for both the Llama and Gemma models, the KL divergence is significantly higher in the first few tokens than for later tokens.

records.verbatim_quote: the refusal-related signal of LRMs drops sharply at the first generated token under harmful queries, which is associated with unsafe response generation.

records.positioning_sentence: Qi et al. (2406.05946) and Yang et al. (2609.18471) both show the first generated token(s) carry the safety decision, but both require a base-model or instruction-tuned counterpart for the comparison; our refusal-commitment trajectory over the first 8 tokens is computed from a single checkpoint with no parent reference, enabling cross-family comparison where theirs cannot be applied.
